title: Talent Acquisition Partner - GTM Enterprise
description:
Mentimeter is an engagement tool with a clear goal in mind. To make every leader better. Through real-time interactivity and clear visualizations, we get people to participate, engage and become more productive. Transforming all those passive meetings, airless classrooms and drawn out trainings into valuable insights and impactful moments.

We truly believe that you achieve the best results by doing things together. And that successful leaders need to adopt a curious and collaborative mindset in order to get there. So with you at Mentimeter, you’ll be a big part of the ambition to help over 1 billion people listen, learn and work better together.

The role

Great recruitment is felt by everyone it touches - the candidate who gets a thoughtful answer, the hiring manager who feels truly partnered with, and the team that grows stronger with every hire. We're looking for a Talent Acquisition Partner who takes ownership of all three.

As our Talent Acquisition Partner for GTM Enterprise, you'll be the dedicated recruitment partner to our Enterprise sales organization across EMEA. You'll own hiring end-to-end for roles like SDRs, Account Executives, Customer Success Managers and Sales Managers from kickoff to signed offer.

This is a 12 -month contract with real ownership from day one. Within your first few months you'll be running 7 - 10 roles in parallel, and hiring managers will see you as a clear, proactive and structured partner. Within six months, you'll own the GTM Enterprise hiring plan, be a trusted voice in Sales Directors' hiring-planning conversations, and have left your mark on how we hire in sales.

Responsibilities

• Own full-cycle recruitment for GTM Enterprise roles across EMEA, from kickoff to offer

• Partner closely with hiring managers to define needs, align expectations and run structured, high-quality processes

• Build proactive pipelines for current and future needs, especially for business-critical roles

• Identify talent risks and upcoming changes in the organization, and act on them early

• Run internal recruitment processes during team changes, internal moves and promotions

• Coach hiring managers on structured, unbiased interviewing and recruitment best practice

• Use data, insights and AI to keep improving hiring quality, speed and candidate experience

 

What will help you succeed

We think you'll thrive here if you:

• Have around 6 years of experience as a Talent Acquisition Partner or Recruiter, ideally including time in a SaaS scale-up hiring sales and GTM roles in Stockholm

• Have owned full-cycle recruitment for multiple complex roles at once, balancing competing priorities and stakeholders

• Know how to influence hiring managers through structure, data and being one step ahead

• Are a hands-on sourcer who knows how to get the most out of LinkedIn Recruiter and Hiring Assistant

• Already use AI in your day-to-day work to multiply your own output and have improved recruitment processes or tools as a result

• Communicate confidently in English, both written and spoken

It's a bonus if you have a background in RPO or high-volume agency recruitment, experience hiring for both volume and mid-senior roles, or have supported internal mobility or succession processes.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is proactive, structured and candidate-first. You ramp up fast, stay calm under pressure, and bring solutions. You're confident sharing a different perspective with hiring managers, and you know when it matters most. You never trade candidate experience for speed.

Why this role, why now

This role exists to build strong teams that support our sales recruitment and long-term growth. You'll see a direct line between your work and where Mentimeter is a year from now.

You'll join an experienced, collaborative TA team with clear ways of working and shared ownership, and a modern toolkit: Greenhouse, Claude, Alva Labs, LinkedIn Hiring Assistant, Notion, Slack and Google Workspace

title: Senior Channel Partner Manager, Global Advisory / GSI

description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is building institutional partnerships with the GSI (Global System Integrators), Big-Four consulting firms, and global advisory firms that shape finance transformation, ERP modernization, and technology decisions for the CFOs and finance leaders we serve. These organizations are often in the room when enterprise clients are redesigning their finance stack, selecting technology, or moving from strategy into implementation.

This portfolio spans the largest global professional services firms (e.g., Deloitte) and GSIs (e.g., Infosys). They are complex organizations with distinct service lines (e.g., ERP, Tech Modernization, Finance Transformation) each with its own leadership, incentives, and economics, so earning credibility inside one is as much about navigating the firm as it is about the relationship.

This role will own Ramp's relationship with that network of firms, building firm-specific go-to-market motions that can include executive engagement, account mapping, co-sell, implementation alignment, thought leadership, and events. Ramp's relationships here are early and largely informal today, so this person will be responsible for the relationship, the partnership thesis, and the operating motion that makes a firm a meaningful Ramp partner over time.

What You'll Do

- Own Ramp's relationships with a portfolio of the largest global professional services, GSIs, and consulting firms, serving as the primary relationship owner

- Map each firm and build credibility with the partners, practice leaders, alliance teams and client-service teams who matter most

- Turn executive introductions into structured partnerships, developing the partnership thesis, executive sponsor plan, target practices and client wedge for each firm

- Negotiate and close the first formal agreements between Ramp and these firms

- Build market-facing proof points with Ramp's leadership, marketing and product teams, including executive events, thought leadership and shared client stories

- Coordinate execution across Ramp, bringing the right Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, Product, AI Solutions and executive sponsors into each firm relationship

- Establish and maintain the operating cadence: relationship maps, firm plans, account maps and next steps

What You Need

- 6+ years of experience in consulting, alliances, partnerships or an adjacent role. Time inside a top-tier professional services or global consulting firm (e.g., McKinsey, Bain, BCG, Deloitte) is strongly preferred.

- Exceptional executive presence. You can hold a room with senior leaders, earn trust quickly, and be trusted to represent Ramp in meetings without support

- Fluency in how large, matrixed professional services firms actually work, including how practices are incentivized and how a technology partner earns internal endorsement

- Proven ability to run many workstreams and complex stakeholder management

- A builder's instinct. You are energized by an empty page, comfortable without a playbook, and bring structure to ambi

title: GenAI Application Engineer

Diseñar, prototipar y entregar aplicaciones funcionales potenciadas con inteligencia artificial -como asistentes, tableros interactivos y soluciones con componentes generativos- en ciclos cortos de desarrollo. Competencias Clave

Resultados Esperados

Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth , we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Our mission is to deliver seamless event experiences through powerful SaaS solutions and a client-first approach.
Role Purpose
To personally drive new business generation for the time being, while leading existing-account commercial management and Customer Success across the portfolio - building a scalable, predictable revenue engine while protecting strong customer relationships. This is a new SLT seat created alongside the Marketing Director as JET's commercial function is split into two dedicated leadership roles. The role carries commercial/revenue accountability and operates as a member of the Senior Leadership Team.

• Develop and maintain accurate sales forecasts and pipeline reporting.

• Identify risks and opportunities early; create recovery plans when targets are at risk.

• Report revenue performance to the MD and SLT.

• Accurate forecasting with no revenue surprises.

• Early identification and management of risk.

title: Controller

At SafeLease , we're rethinking how P&C insurance is sold in an age of technological change. We believe the industry's biggest inefficiencies aren't technical problems - they're structural ones. And we're building the team to tackle them.
SafeLease is a profitable insurance business that designs, underwrites, and distributes specialty coverage for commercial property owners and their tenants. Most insurance companies either distribute products or bear the risk - we do both. We back our policies with our own capital, which means we control the full stack: product design, tech, and the speed at which we move. That end-to-end ownership lets us offer customers real flexibility, saving time and money for more than 4,000 properties insured for billions in value nationwide.
We're a team of 85, growing over 100% annually, and we've done it without sacrificing profitability or culture. Here, you'll get high discretion and a wide aperture of problems to solve. We embrace the newest technologies, move fast together, and operate with the intensity of a small company where every person's work is visible. If you're looking for a place to sharpen your craft alongside people who take their work seriously, you'll fit right in.
About The Role
SafeLease is hiring a Controller to lead all accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls across the organization - with full ownership spanning our Managing General Agent (MGA) operations and our surplus lines insurance carrier. The role owns dual-track reporting: U.S. GAAP financial statements for SafeLease and its consolidated entities, and statutory financial statements filed with state insurance regulators under NAIC Statutory Accounting Principles. The ideal candidate combines a Big Four audit foundation with hands-on accounting experience inside an insurance carrier, and a track record of building and scaling finance functions in a high-growth environment. • Manage statutory reporting and regulatory filings: NAIC Schedules F (reinsurance), P (loss reserves), D (investments), and T (premium by state); Risk-Based Capital (RBC) calculations; IRIS ratios; and domiciliary and non-admitted / surplus lines state filings.

• Oversee MGA accounting under the NAIC Managing General Agents Act (Model #225), including premium trust / fiduciary accounts, the MGA-to-carrier reporting cycle, and quarterly accounting packages submitted to the carrier in a form usable for completion of the Annual Statement.

• Design, implement, and maintain robust internal controls and financial policies that scale with organizational growth (SOX-style frameworks preferred).

• Lead the annual statutory and GAAP audits and serve as the primary liaison with external auditors, tax advisors, state insurance examiners, and the engaged actuary.

• Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing accounting team; establish best-in-class processes and a culture of continuous improvement.

• Manage consolidated financial reporting across SafeLease entities, including intercompany transactions and eliminations between the MGA and the carrier.

• Partner with the CEO and senior leadership to provide financial insights, variance analysis, and strategic recommendations.

title: Applied Research Engineer
description:
ABOUT US

Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. We have raised over $175M with support from top-notch venture capital firms and more than 18 strategic investors: industry leaders in construction, building products manufacturing, and distribution.

Higharc is seeking a hands-on Applied Research Engineer to turn our spatial AI research into capabilities that homebuyers and builders use. You'll join our Platform R&D team, taking models that have proven themselves in research and shipping them into the product.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Our team builds AI that understands homes, and our generative floor plan engine has moved from proof of concept to a core workflow in Higharc's product. You'll own the applied side of that work. The research team hands you a defined problem and a metric. You train and adapt the models, build the pipelines around them, and ship a component that meets the product's latency and cost budget.

You'll work inside an architecture that already exists. The engine, the schema, and the evaluation frameworks are in place, and your job is to make them faster, reproducible, and easy for others to build on.

Expect to:

- Build the component layer around our layout synthesis engine: a documented API contract, a service the product can call, and an evaluation gate that runs on every change.

- Turn model retraining into a one-command job, with benchmarks built in and results the whole team can read.

- Own the latency and cost budgets for learned capabilities.

- Extend core research into new capabilities, such as multi-story plans and real-time editing.

- Partner with infrastructure engineers on MLOps and deployment, and mentor researchers and interns on engineering practices.

- Share your work in writing through weekly status updates, clear pull requests, and design notes before big changes.

ABOUT YOU

You're happiest when a model you worked on is running in the product. You like taking a well-defined problem with a metric attached and closing it, and you improve an existing codebase without feeling the need to rewrite it. You think about what a 45-second wait means for a user before you think about what it means for a benchmark. You're honest about evaluation: you can tell when a result is an artifact of the test set, and you'd rather report a regression in writing than hide it behind a demo.

Most of your collaborators are remote and some are part-time, so writing things down comes naturally to you. You can go from a research conversation to a product conversation to an infrastructure conversation in the same week and be understood in all three. You also know enough about buildings to see that a bedroom door opening onto a kitchen is wrong before any metric tells you.

You have:

- 5+ years of professional software development, including at least 2 years training and shipping ML models to real users

- Taken at least one model end to end: data preparation, training, evaluation, serving, and the integration that put it in front of users

- Fluency in Python and PyTorch (TensorFlow or Keras is fine if you're ready to move to PyTorch)

- Built or maintained an evaluation harness or benchmark and used it to gate changes

- Packaged a model behind an API (FastAPI or similar) and owned its latency and cost

- A master's degree in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or equivalent shipped work (a PhD is not required)

- Comfort working remotely with a team on US Eastern hours

A major plus if you also bring:

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
ABOUT COLUMN

For companies building financial technology and transforming the financial services space, the biggest bottleneck to their growth and innovation is often the underlying banks and infrastructure stack they rely on. We have spent our careers founding and scaling companies like Plaid, Square, Meta, Blend, and Affirm, and have seen this problem firsthand - builders and developers needing to partner with traditional banks, and creating API and abstraction layers over the patchwork that is the bank, its core, and many other vendors. All of this results in a complex (and often expensive) banking supply chain involving a user, fintech, BaaS middleware provider, bank, core and the Federal Reserve.

At Column, we set out to simplify and fix this. We are a bank and a software company built from the ground up, offering builders and developers technology-forward banking solutions that cut out the hundreds of vendors, middleware providers, and abstraction layers. This means a safer, more transparent, and less costly banking supply chain. Come build with us!

The opportunity:
We're a lean, experienced engineering team, and we're hiring our first Forward Deployed Engineer. You'll define what this role looks like at Column.

As an FDE, you'll work with customers to understand their problems in depth and help them build new products on Column's APIs. What you learn in the field will feed directly into how our engineering team improves the platform.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll write code, debug payment flows and design integrations, and you'll spend a lot of time on-site with customers. You'll get deep exposure to the full banking stack, from our APIs down to the Federal Reserve.

This role is based in our Presidio office in San Francisco, with frequent travel to customer sites in the US and abroad. You will report directly to William, the CEO.

Read more about Life @ Column and our hiring process here https://www.notion.so/Hiring-at-Column-b8d9b2628317491989d4713091b6bb68?pvs=21. 🚀

What you'll do:

- Work directly with our partner’s engineering teams to design, build and launch products with Column's state-of-the-art banking stack

- Act as the technical owner for strategic customers from onboarding to launch, unblocking them on architecture, ledgering, reconciliation and edge cases in money movement

- Write production-quality code, that speeds up integrations and grows into reusable product

- Turn patterns from the field into product and platform improvements, working closely with engineering to shape our APIs, docs and developer experience

- Advise customers on how to build safe, compliant and resilient financial products in a regulated environment

- Represent Column in conversations with customer executives and engineering leaders, and build trusted, long-term relationships

What we're looking for:

- Need to be fluent in either Spanish, French or Russian.

- Strong engineering fundamentals, ideally with experience in backend systems, APIs or infrastructure

- Product thinking: you look past the immediate ask to the underlying problem and the best solution, for the customer and for Column

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills. You can explain complex systems clearly to an engineer or an executive

- Executive presence and the confidence to lead high-stakes customer conversations

- Strong project management skills. You can run several customer engagements at once and keep each one moving

- A self-starter mindset. You're comfortable with ambiguity and with building process where none exists yet

- Experience with payments, banking or financial infrastructure is a plus

WHAT YOU’LL GET FROM US:

- 🏥 Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans, including options that are 100% covered by Column for you and 100% covered for your dependents!

- 🐣 Comprehensive family planning and fertility benefits via partnership with Carrot, including reimbursement of up to $20,000 in qualified expenses

Engineering the sub-millisecond decision engine that powers 200 million daily ad interactions

The Demand Core team builds the infrastructure that determines which of our thousands of active advertising campaigns are relevant to a user the moment they open our ad unit Playtime. At our scale, system latency is a business failure, downtime means advertisers stop spending, users stop earning rewards, and publisher revenue stalls. You will build and operate the services that power these decisions 200 million times every day.

Go microservices load the active ad campaign catalog into memory, evaluating 40+ targeting constraints and 30+ real-time signals, geo, fraud status, budget caps to rank potential user performance in milliseconds. Beyond campaign distribution, the team owns the entire ad interaction chain: processing clicks, views, MMP postbacks from Adjust and AppsFlyer, and in-app events that trigger rewards. These events are broadcasted through a hybrid messaging architecture using SNS/SQS and Kafka, directly powering our advertiser dashboards, publisher reward payouts, and ad campaign scoring pipelines, all backed by DynamoDB.

Production Golang Systems Expertise: You bring 5+ years of backend development experience, including at least 3 years writing Go in production distributed environments. High-Throughput Event Streaming: You have hands-on experience designing asynchronous microservice communication using event buses like Kafka, SQS/SNS, and Kinesis. You will build pipelines to collect billions of daily API events and aggregate them into our data lake for sub-second querying.

High-Scale Data & API Optimization: You understand database internals and low-level web standards (HTTP protocol, Encoding, Regular Expressions). You will optimize queries across hundreds of terabytes of data across DynamoDB, MySQL, Druid, and Athena to reduce API response times and expose transparent, well-documented open APIs to enterprise partners.

Data Science & Algorithmic Integration: You quickly grasp complex technical topics and applied mathematics. You will partner directly with our Data Science team to translate and integrate machine learning algorithms into adjoe’s core application, optimizing real-time ad targeting.

Collaborative Technical Communication: You communicate fluently and precisely in spoken and written English. You will actively participate in peer code reviews and technical knowledge sharing across an international backend engineering team.

Plus: Infrastructure & Cloud Tooling: Hands-on experience with Terraform (Infrastructure as Code), Docker containerization, or serverless infrastructure.

The Firefox team is a community of engineers who care deeply about delivering the fastest, friendliest, most usable browser possible. We are responsible for making the things you see in the browser work securely, quickly, and well! The Desktop integrations team is a cross-functional team that focuses on updates, installs and integrating Firefox with different OS platforms. As part of the Desktop Integrations team, you will be responsible for all things related to OS integration (particularly Windows and macOS) and helping us grow our user base.

Our team is geographically distributed, and working in the open is the norm. We contribute to the code driving the Firefox browser on all desktop platforms.

About the role:

A Software Engineer is an early-career individual contributor who is growing in their ability to take on more complex tasks. At Mozilla , this role involves working on engineering projects that typically span several weeks and require collaboration with peers. Software Engineers at this level contribute to implementation, ask thoughtful questions, and raise blockers early. • Assist in the development and maintenance of Firefox features related to installs, updates, and OS integrations.

• Engage with a distributed team and contribute positively to our open and inclusive work environment.

• Some experience with systems-level programming on a major platform (e.g., Windows, macOS).

• Proficiency with C/C++ programming.

• Willingness to communicate clearly, ask questions, and seek feedback.

• Ability to contribute to collaborative projects and steadily build up your technical and problem-solving skills.

• A growth mindset and enthusiasm for contributing to impactful software.

Bonus Points

• Exposure to or experience with Rust.

• Familiarity with Linux, or macOS internals.

• Exposure to or familiarity with native Windows or macOS APIs (such as Win32 or Cocoa)

• Previous participation in open source projects or a strong interest in learning how to contribute.

title: Production Engineer
description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with an fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

 

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision https://www.monumental.co/our-vision/and company https://www.monumental.co/about/. You might enjoy Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2-Q2F0Fcx4A, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DOo8n19XEns.

About the role

Monumental are already deploying robots into the real world at scale, building beautiful, bespoke homes. Our robots are on sites across the Netherlands and the UK and will be in the US within a year. Every deployment teaches us something about our hardware; you’ll push our R&D fleet to become one ready for large-series production: you'll own taking us from tens of robots a year to hundreds, and then thousands. You'll also keep that growing fleet deployable, and making design changes yourself to improve reliability and serviceability.

Scaling a fleet means solving whatever is in the way: limited space, no clear production process, lead times we can't live with and modules that don't survive the harsh conditions of a construction site. You’ll be expected to wear many hats; we’re looking for people who are genuinely excited to lead these efforts.

Our robots are built from modules at every level of maturity, so expect to work with the hardware R&D team at early stages of development to validate R&D designs as fast as we can. In parallel, you'll be in the workshop determining how we assemble them: the processes, the fixtures, the production space itself, getting the very best out of our Amsterdam facilities.

For more context on building hardware at Monumental, read Niall’s Substack: I quit my job and moved country to make robots that will fix Europe’s housing crisis. https://open.substack.com/pub/buildmonumental/p/i-quit-my-job-and-moved-country-to?r=68ngjs&utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=post%20viewer

What you'll do

- Bottom line, you'll own increasing our quarterly production from 30 sets of robot systems to 100 within a year. This is a challenge. You'll be building the production capabilities at Monumental rather than inheriting them, and you'll do it alongside engineers and technicians who care a great deal about getting this right.

- Take prototypes through to production-ready modules. Find and address design flaws, validate improvements, and push these modules to production.

- Assembling modules, understand the friction slowing production, and address issues yourself along with the hardware team.

- Develop fixtures, jigs and light automation solutions to support module assembly.

- Find production processes that bring minimal value when done in-house. Work with external suppliers to outsource them, while maintaining production quality.

- Produce drawings, assembly instructions and quality checks to make sure our modules are integrated together and our robots are brought up with no errors.

title: Policy Principal - DMEE
description:
About Advanced Energy United

Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country.

We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy.

If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more-and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team.

We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously.

Position Description

Advanced Energy United (United) is currently seeking a Policy Principal to help shape political strategy on our Decisionmaker Education and Engagement team (DMEE).

The DMEE team builds relationships with governors, state regulators, state energy officials, and policymakers to equip them with the information and resources to understand advanced energy products, services, and business models - as well as the policy and political solutions we need to unleash them. Through political events, conferences, and business roundtables, United engages key decision-makers around the benefits that advanced energy technologies and services can provide to their constituents and helps to solve the challenges in obtaining these benefits.

Reporting directly to the Policy Senior Director, the Policy Principal will cultivate relationships and inform strategies to help achieve the DMEE team’s goals.

The ideal candidate is energized by thinking about how political dynamics and relationships affect energy policy decisions. Successful applicants must have experience related to political and/or advocacy campaigns, bolstered by exceptional project management, relationship building, and communication skills. While you do not need to be a state energy policy expert to be considered for this role, strong candidates will possess an interest in energy policy issues and be comfortable with communicating with decision-makers regarding United’s state policy priorities. The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, proactive, comfortable with ambiguity, and flexible. Candidates will need to travel to meet with key stakeholders approximately 1-2 times per quarter.

Responsibilities

• Own the political strategy for building relationships with key decision-makers in a portfolio of Midwest states

• Develop effective communication strategies that incorporate state-specific energy outlooks and political landscapes and deploy those strategies to represent United in front of state decision-makers

• Build, maintain, and own relationships with key stakeholders, including policymakers, advocacy groups, coalitions, industry experts, and regulators

• Use project management tools and systems effectively to deliver success on both short and long-term goals.

• Maintain and organize information to contribute to program knowledge management and retention

• Communicate campaign

title: Security Engineer, Vulnerability Management & Security Operations
description:
ABOUT LIVEKIT

LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

Our customers trust us with audio, video and data belonging to their own end users, so a security failure on our side puts their data and their business at risk. We are hiring a Security Engineer to build and run our vulnerability management and security operations program. Vulnerability management is a core capability for keeping our security posture strong as the platform and the company grow: knowing what we run, finding what is exposed, and getting the right fixes shipped quickly. It also underpins our customer commitments and the compliance programs we are building. Our program is early, and you will shape it. You will join a small Trust team that covers security, IT and compliance, and you will own this program end to end from your first week.

YOU'LL THRIVE AT LIVEKIT IF YOU

- think like both a builder and a breaker, and understand security from first principles

- take an automation-first and pragmatic approach to risk mitigation

- translate security concerns into engineering action

- can clearly explain complex technical concepts to others

- are a fast learner and thrive in ambiguity

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Select, deploy and operationalize scanning tooling across our production assets.

- Run vulnerability management end to end: triage, severity in our environment, owner assignment, remediation SLAs and reporting.

- Build engineering-first triage and remediation workflows that fit how our engineering teams already work, and automate the routing and follow-up.

- Build a remediation dashboard that engineering and leadership read and act on.

- Automate collection of the vulnerability management evidence our compliance programs depend on, in partnership with our Compliance team.

- Build automation, including agentic tooling, that removes manual security operations work and keeps pace with engineering growth.

WHO YOU ARE

- 5+ years in security engineering, security operations or software engineering, with a significant share of that focused on security.

- Hands-on experience building or running a vulnerability management program or software security tooling (SCA, container, cloud or host scanning).

- An engineering-first approach to triage and remediation: you get findings fixed by making the fix easy to ship.

- The judgment to set a finding's real severity in our environment, using CVSS as one input.

- Strong scripting and automation skills in a language such as Go or Python, and comfort reading infrastructure as code such as Terraform.

- A pragmatic approach to risk: you can explain why a finding matters to the business and how fast it needs to be fixed.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience with real-time media, networking or WebRTC systems.

- Experience supporting compliance audits such as HIPAA, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001 or SOC 2.

- Incident response or application security experience.

- Experience in AI security, such as securing LLM applications or agent infrastructure.

OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU

- An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world

- Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers

- Competitive salary and equity package

- Health, dental, and vision benefits

- Flexible vacation policy

LiveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

title: Accountant
description:
ACCOUNTANT

Permanent employee · Full-time · Berlin (HQ)

OUR MISSION FOR YOU

Help us build an in-house accounting function from the ground up. trawa is bringing its bookkeeping in-house, and you'll be one of the people who makes that work: clean books, on time, every month.

trawa enables mid-sized companies to access green, intelligent energy. We're a hyper-growth energy-tech company with strong team growth, backed by Balderton Capital, Speedinvest and Headline. Our business model sits at the intersection of energy, tech, and finance, which makes our accounting more complex and more interesting than a typical start-up ledger.

You'll start hands-on with day-to-day accounting and keep the books clean as volumes grow. At the same time, you'll spot the manual steps in your work and get room to automate them. You'll also be part of our ERP rollout. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to own their area, not just process it.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Accounts Payable

- Process, check, and post incoming invoices from Moss into DATEV, including correct VAT treatment

- Handle expenses and credit card bookings

- Maintain vendor master data and keep supplier accounts reconciled

- Prepare payment runs

Month-End Support

- Reconcile bank transactions

- Prepare accruals and reconciliations for your areas

- Support the monthly close and year-end, working with our auditors

- Keep documentation GoBD-compliant and audit-ready

- Partner with Ops, Procurement and budget owners to resolve invoice and cost questions

Build & Improve

- Spot manual steps in your processes and automate them

- Contribute to our ERP rollout

WHO YOU ARE

Must-haves

- 2 to 4 years of hands-on bookkeeping experience, ideally in accounts payable

- Comfortable when processes don't exist yet. You help create them instead of waiting for them

- Solid understanding of German GAAP (HGB) and VAT basics

- Precise and fast. You care about getting it right and getting it done

- Analytical and confident in Excel or Google Sheets for reconciliations

- Fluent in English

Nice-to-haves

- German is a strong plus (B1 or better): most of our vendor invoices and much of our supplier communication are in German

- Experience in a fast-growing company (start-up or scale-up), or at a tax firm serving start-up clients

- Hands-on with DATEV Rechnungswesen and DATEV Unternehmen online (DUO)

- Training as Steuerfachangestellte/r or Kaufmann/-frau

- Experience with Moss or similar spend management tools

- Automation experience or strong tech curiosity: you've built workflows with n8n, Zapier, or Make, or used Claude Code or similar AI tools

YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

Month 1: Learn

- Understand our business model, our accounting setup, and our tools (Moss, DATEV). Take over your first recurring bookings.

Month 2: Own

- Run accounts payable and bank postings independently. Support your first month-end close.

Month 3: Improve

- Deliver your areas on time each month. Propose and ship your first automation or process improvement.

THE TEAM

You'll join a fast-growing Finance team of around ten people across Accounting, Billing, Collections, FP&A, Treasury, and Strategic Finance. You'll work closely with colleagues across these areas and see how your bookings flow into cash and planning. You'll also work cross-functionally with Business Operations, Energy, and other departments.

WHY TRAWA?

- Real ownership from day one. You build the accounting function from the start, not just maintain one

- Learn fast from an experienced Senior Accountant, with direct contact to our hands-on Finance leadership team

- A uniquely complex problem space at the intersection of energy, tech, and finance, plus a PwC audit and an ERP rollout

- An AI-first Finance team that embraces new tools and ways of working

- Clear growth path within our career framework: grow towards Senior Accountant, or specialise in revenue accounting or finance systems as we scale

- Flexible working, 30 vacation days,

When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.

At Parexel , we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.
Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel , contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.
The Project Leadership function at Parexel is a critical part of driving success for our clients and advancing clinical research projects. As a part of the Global Project Leadership organization, your work has a direct impact on the projects, teams, and clients you work with, while helping deliver projects to the benefit of the patients we serve.

Parexel ’s defined Biotech Division offers opportunities for seasoned Project Management professionals with a strong background running global clinical trials in a variety of therapeutics. This group focuses specifically on Biotech clients and providing all areas of support to accommodate their unique needs. This is a great opportunity for those in the industry who prefer the flexibility, creatively and problem-solving mindset to successfully support this type of clients.
Parexel has opportunities at the Project Leader (PM), Senior Project Leader (SPM) and Project Director level for candidates with experience leading global studies in a variety of therapeutics including Oncology (Hematology), Respiratory / General Medicine and Obesity/Endocrine
Individuals selected for these roles will provide leadership to project teams and manage the day-to-day operations while striving to achieve operational excellence through on time delivery within budget and to the highest quality with the goal to exceed client expectations
Successful candidates possess an undergraduate degree in a clinical or health related field: advanced degree preferred, along with at minimum, 2+ years' experience leading Global Clinal Trials in Project Management within a CRO (preferred), Biotech or Pharma company. These positions also require experience in project scheduling, managing resources and budgets and coordinating team activities, as well as experience with the full clinical development process through regulatory submissions. Additional years of experience will be required for the more senior roles of Senior Project Leader, Associate Project Director, and Project Director.

To excel in this role, flexibility, problem solving capabilities and strategic vision are qualities that propel our Project Leadership team member’s growth. In addition, you need to be detailed-oriented, computer proficient and possess superior interpersonal and organizational skills.
